source_verification.note: Source text layer is visually encoded/garbled in extraction, but the seven pages were directly inspected from the canonical Library PDF and reconstructed by meaning/function. Do not use historical chat paraphrases as source.

units.function: Invite the family to revisit the 24-day experience on one evening between Christmas and New Year, with three low-pressure reflection prompts.
mechanics: Choose one evening between Christmas and New Year.
Optionally light a candle and sit together.
Revisit favourite moments from the 24 days.
Ask what changed for them, explicitly allowing very small shifts.
units.tone_job: Warm retrospective without therapy language, grand transformation claims or school-style debrief.
units.humor_room: Keep the source chocolate-disappearing joke in a natural Polish form.
protected_truth: The timing window is between Christmas and New Year.
Small changes count.
No claim that the activities necessarily changed anyone.

units.function: First half of a family promise: kindness, pausing when somebody needs room, quiet support, noticing tiny joys and making room for laughter.
mechanics: Read or adapt together as a shared family promise.
units.tone_job: Specific, warm and human. Avoid ceremonial or therapeutic wording.
units.humor_room: Patience as a rare mythical creature and badly timed laughter are source comic beats.
protected_truth: Support may be quiet and wordless.
Tiny joys and private family victories matter.
Laughter is welcomed, including badly timed laughter.

units.function: Second half of family promise: respect dreams, support one another, care for and repair shared peace, keep choosing one another with warmth, honesty and humor.
mechanics: Continue the shared promise from p99.
units.tone_job: Grounded family commitment, not motivational manifesto.
units.humor_room: Quietly googling an unusual dream is a source comic beat.
protected_truth: Dreams include brave and strange ones.
Repair after wobble is expected, not failure.
Family home is framed as a place worth returning to.
Presence/togetherness is the closing value.

units.function: Offer a closing wish that the small calm, laughter, kindness and affection practiced during Advent continue into ordinary family life after the season.
mechanics: Read as a short closing passage.
units.tone_job: Poetic but natural Polish, stripped of imported spiritual-light rhetoric where it would sound artificial.
units.humor_room: Keep the source joke about decorations refusing to fit back into the box.
protected_truth: Carry the good from Advent into ordinary mornings and conversations.
Kindness and shared laughter remain central.
No guaranteed emotional outcome.

units.function: Happy Makers letter: reaching Day 24 is framed as a beginning; laughing, pausing, listening or simply sitting quietly together is enough.
mechanics: Direct letter from Happy Makers to the family.
units.tone_job: Warm, concise and non-preachy. Replace magic/light claims with concrete family-life language.
units.humor_room: May use small domestic callbacks, but no fake youth slang.
protected_truth: Completion is not treated as the end of the habits.
Ordinary small shared moments are sufficient.
No perfection standard.

units.function: Carry warmth, patience and small joy into the year ahead; when life becomes busy, remember how to return to stillness and one another.
units.tone_job: Concrete memory of reusable actions, not mindfulness doctrine.
units.humor_room: A small family-life interruption can replace abstract light rhetoric if needed.
protected_truth: The practices can be reused beyond December.
The source encourages returning to one another when life is busy.
Do not guarantee that presence makes the world better.

units.function: Thank the family for every pause, laugh and shared breath, then sign off from Happy Makers with love/gratitude.
units.tone_job: Earned warmth without syrup or mystical glow language.
units.humor_room: No extra joke required; ending may be simple.
protected_truth: Thank the family for participating.
Keep gratitude and affectionate sign-off.
Do not strengthen to a spiritual or wellbeing promise.
